# staubliTX2trajectories.py

You can view and download this file on Github: [staubliTX2trajectories.py](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/tree/master/python/Examples/robotics/staubliTX2trajectories.py)

```{code-block} python
:linenos:

#+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
# This is an EXUDYN example
#
# Details:  A Staubli TX2-90L (exudyn.robotics.models.ManipulatorStaubliTX2_90L) as a kinematic tree with PD control of
#           its joints, following a trajectory of four profiles: point to point in joint space with constant
#           accelerations (ProfileConstantAcceleration) and with polynomials of degree 5 (ProfilePolynomial5), a
#           straight line of the tool in Cartesian space with the joint coordinates by the analytic inverse kinematics
#           (ProfileCartesianLinear), and back by a polynomial of degree 5. The control by Robot.SetControl and
#           Robot.PreStepControl, without compensation of gravity; sensors of the joint angles and of the tool
#           position, the deviation of the tool from the straight line printed. The meshes of the URDF of the robot by
#           urdfImport.AddURDFgraphics if the local robot data set is found; the robot with these graphics is then
#           saved by Robot.SaveToHDF5 to solution/staubliTX2_90L.h5, and loaded from there by
#           Robot.LoadFromHDF5 when the data set is not found (h5py and scipy needed); without
#           both, simple link graphics.
#
# Author:   Johannes Gerstmayr
# Date:     2026-11-05
#
# Copyright:This file is part of Exudyn. Exudyn is free software. You can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the Exudyn license. See 'LICENSE.txt' for more details.
#
#+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++

import exudyn as exu
import exudyn.graphics as graphics
import exudyn.itemInterface as eii
from exudyn.robotics import Robot, RobotBase, VRobotBase
from exudyn.basicUtilities import OutputFilePath
from exudyn.robotics.models import ManipulatorStaubliTX2_90L, LinkDict2Robot
from exudyn.robotics.urdfImport import AddURDFgraphics
from exudyn.robotics.motion import Trajectory, ProfileConstantAcceleration, ProfilePolynomial5, ProfileCartesianLinear
import exudyn.cMath as cMath #the math functions of the C++ code, the same bits on every platform
import numpy as np
import os

SC = exu.SystemContainer()
mbs = SC.AddSystem()

robotDict = ManipulatorStaubliTX2_90L()
robot = LinkDict2Robot(robotDict)
#the meshes of the URDF, if the repository CommonData_git is beside this one (internal, #3352), or give the path here
robotDataPath = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), '..', '..', '..', '..', 'CommonData_git', 'data', 'Exudyn', 'robotics', 'URDF')
urdf = robotDict['urdfGraphics']
urdfFile = os.path.join(robotDataPath, urdf['file'])
#the robot with its meshes as HDF5 file
robotFile = OutputFilePath('solution/staubliTX2_90L.h5', 'staubliTX2trajectories')
try:
    import h5py, scipy #needed by Robot.SaveToHDF5 and LoadFromHDF5
    hasHDF5 = True
except ImportError:
    hasHDF5 = False
if os.path.exists(urdfFile):
    AddURDFgraphics(robot, urdfFile, urdf['links'], baseLinkName=urdf['baseLink'])
    if hasHDF5:
        robot.SaveToHDF5(robotFile)
        exu.Print('the robot with its meshes is saved to', robotFile)
elif hasHDF5 and os.path.exists(robotFile):
    robot = Robot()
    robot.LoadFromHDF5(robotFile)
    exu.Print('the robot with its meshes is loaded from', robotFile)
else:
    exu.Print('the URDF meshes were not found at', urdfFile, '; download the package from', urdf['source'],
              'into', robotDataPath, '; the example continues with simple link graphics')
    robot.base = RobotBase(visualization=VRobotBase(graphicsData=[graphics.Cylinder([0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0.3], 0.12, graphics.color.grey)]))

#the trajectory: joint space, then a straight line of the tool, then back
q0 = np.array([0, 0.5, 1.4, 0, 1.2, 0])
q1 = np.array([0.8, 0.2, 1.7, 0.5, 0.9, -0.5])
q2 = np.array([-0.6, 0.6, 1.2, -0.3, 1.0, 0.8])
chain = robot.GetKinematicChain()
lineStart = chain.ToolHT(q2)
lineEnd = exu.HT(rotation=np.array(lineStart.rotation), translation=np.array(lineStart.translation) + [0.25, 0.3, -0.15])
trajectory = Trajectory(initialCoordinates=q0, initialTime=0.25)
trajectory.Add(ProfileConstantAcceleration(q1, 1.))
trajectory.Add(ProfilePolynomial5(q2, 1.))
trajectory.Add(ProfileCartesianLinear(robot, lineEnd, 1., timeLaw='polynomial5'))
trajectory.Add(ProfilePolynomial5(q0, 1.))

robotDict = robot.CreateKinematicTree(mbs)
oKT = robotDict['objectKinematicTree']
mbs.SetNodeParameter(robotDict['nodeGeneric'], 'initialCoordinates', q0) #start at rest on the trajectory
robot.SetControl(trajectory, compensation=None) #compensation='static' adds the static torques of gravity
mbs.SetPreStepUserFunction(robot.PreStepControl)

toolPosition = list(robot.tool.HT.translation)
sTool = mbs.AddSensor(eii.SensorKinematicTree(objectNumber=oKT, linkNumber=5, localPosition=toolPosition,
                                               storeInternal=True, outputVariableType=exu.OutputVariableType.Position))
sJoints = mbs.AddSensor(eii.SensorNode(nodeNumber=robotDict['nodeGeneric'], storeInternal=True,
                                       outputVariableType=exu.OutputVariableType.Coordinates))
mbs.Assemble()

tEnd = 4.5
simulationSettings = exu.SimulationSettings()
simulationSettings.timeIntegration.numberOfSteps = 4500
simulationSettings.timeIntegration.endTime = tEnd
simulationSettings.solution.file.writePeriod = 0.01
simulationSettings.solution.sensors.writePeriod = 0.005
simulationSettings.timeIntegration.verboseMode = 1
simulationSettings.show.computationTime = True
SC.visualizationSettings.connectors.showJointAxes = True
SC.visualizationSettings.nodes.show = False
SC.visualizationSettings.window.renderWindowSize = [1600, 1200]

SC.renderer.Start()
SC.renderer.DoIdleTasks()
mbs.SolveDynamic(simulationSettings)
SC.renderer.DoIdleTasks()
SC.renderer.Stop()

#the tool on the straight line: its distance from the line during the Cartesian profile
data = mbs.GetSensorStoredData(sTool)
pStart = np.array(lineStart.translation)
direction = (np.array(lineEnd.translation) - pStart)/cMath.norm(np.array(lineEnd.translation) - pStart)
onLine = (data[:, 0] >= 2.25) & (data[:, 0] <= 3.25)
deviation = max(cMath.norm((p - pStart) - ((p - pStart) @ direction)*direction) for p in data[onLine, 1:4])
exu.Print('largest distance of the tool from the straight line:', deviation, 'm')

mbs.PlotSensor(sJoints, components=list(range(6)), labels=['q' + str(i) for i in range(6)], title='joint angles')
mbs.SolutionViewer()
```
